candidates.title: BNSF Q3 earnings climb 19.3% as rail freight volumes rise
candidates.excerpt: BNSF’s third-quarter earnings rose 19.3% to $1.73 billion as higher freight volumes and improved operating efficiencies helped offset increased fuel costs. The railroad’s net earnings increased from $1.45 billion in the third quarter of 2025, parent company Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK-B) reported. Railroad operating revenue climbed 14.7% to $6.87 billion, while car and unit volumes rose 3.9%, for the period ended Sept. 30. The results extended BNSF’s earnings growth for the year. Through September, net earnings reached $4.66 billion, up 13% from $4.13 billion in the first nine months of 2025. Berkshire attributed the improvement to higher freight volumes and operating efficiencies, partly offset by rising fuel expenses. BNSF’s railroad operating earnings increased to $2.48 billion in the third quarter from $2.15 billion a year earlier. candidates.excerpt: Evergreen’s 16,556-TEU containership EVER EON transited the Suez Canal on 8 November, marking a significant step in the carrier’s gradual return to the waterway after nearly three years of disruption linked to the Red Sea crisis. According to the Suez Canal Authority (SCA), the 369-metre-long vessel passed through the canal while travelling from the Netherlands to Singapore. EVER EON operates on the Ocean Alliance’s NEU7 service, connecting the Far East with Northwest Europe. The transit follows Evergreen’s recently announced plans to resume Suez Canal sailings, which Container News reported on 6 November. Admiral Ossama Rabiee, Chairman and Managing Director of the SCA, described the transit as a positive development for shipping between Asia and Europe. He also indicated that Evergreen intends to route additional voyages through the canal in the coming period. candidates.excerpt: Australian regulator halts two Angas private credit funds Australia’s corporate regulator has issued interim stop orders against two private credit funds run by Angas Securities, the latest move in its clampdown on the sector. The orders cover the Angas Prime Income Fund and the Angas Direct Mortgage Fund, and bar Angas Securities from offering, issuing, selling or transferring interests in either vehicle. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) said investors in both funds may not have been “adequately informed” about Angas Securities’ financial position and the risks arising from it. The regulator said the funds’ product disclosure statements did not disclose a net asset deficiency, a breach of net tangible asset requirements or a proposed capital raising. ASIC also raised concerns over disclosures to investors in the Angas Prime Income Fund about the fund’s exposure to Bathla Group, the collapsed Sydney-based housing developer. candidates.title: UP No. 5511 begins steam testing
candidates.excerpt: SILVIS, Ill. — Union Pacific 2-10-2 No. 5511 was steamed up today (Friday, Nov. 6) by Railroading Heritage of Midwest America. It is the first time the locomotive has been under steam since 1956. The locomotive, built by Baldwin in 1923, is the sole remaining UP 2-10-2. RRHMA began an extensive rebuilding project after the engine was donated by UP in 2022. The locomotive was retired in 1956, and was last used that year as a stationary boiler for an industry in Ogden, Utah. It was used in filming the Union Pacific motion picture “Last of the Giants” in 1958, but was not under steam at that time. It was then stored in Green River, Wyo., until it was transferred to the UP roundhouse in Cheyenne, Wyo., in 1968. The locomotive, which underwent a hydrostatic test on Sept. 8, was pulled outside the Silvis facility and steamed up for testing. RRHMA has not announced any immediate plans to operate the 2-10-2. — To report news or errors, contact trainsnewswire@firecrown.com.
